exp_info.description: At What's Up I taught English from beginner classes all the way to C1 using presentations, music, roleplay and more. The school had students from all over the world, so I got to experience a lot of variety. At the beginning of every shift I would prepare the classes, but after a while it became second nature to me. The encouragement to develop relationships with students was one of the things that made the environment at the academy very memorable. Overall it was a great experience for me.

I worked in schools for kids and young adults teaching English. Classes ranged from 1-40 students. Before every day started I had to prep the classes as well. A lot of responsibility, but it was an amazing experience.

An Eikaiwa is a type of language conversation class in Japan. People come in informal settings like at cafes and bars and talk to a native speaker. Here I was responsible for "selling myself" to the students and providing high quality lessons day in and day out. Building relationships were also fatal as well as pairing students together matching the same interests and age groups. I also did bar events where I was responsible for 30+ students and had to come up with games and interesting topics.

Je leert vanaf de eerste dag Nederlands te spreken, en we behandelen alledaagse thema's in de les. Binnen dit thema leer je grammatica en veel nieuwe woorden en uitdrukkingen. Natuurlijk wordt er ook aandacht gegeven aan de uitspraak en het culturele leven in Nederland.

This Dutch course is especially for those who need to learn Dutch. For example, for work, because you are going to live in the Netherlands or you have to do business in the Netherlands. The method is based on the book Zichtbaar Nederlands. This method  teaches you to understand the structure and the build up of the language.
You learn to speak Dutch from day one, and we deal with everyday topics in class. Within this theme you learn grammar and many new words and expressions. Of course attention is also given to pronunciation and cultural life in the Netherlands.

teacher_info.about_teacher:
As a teacher, my aim is to encourage you, be patient, and understanding.

My main goal is to help you learn a language effectively and at your own pace, while also enjoying the entirety of the process.

Having fun is part of learning too :)

Still, an important part of mastering any language, is the amount of effort you put in. Not just in terms of the lessons themselves, but the work you do outside them.

That could be reading, listening to podcasts or watching TV shows.

Just taking lessons will make the road to mastering either Norwegian or English arduous.
teacher_info.teaching_style:
My classes will be based on two methods primarily:

1. Informal lessons: During these lessons, the atmosphere is relaxed and fun. The aim is to speak as much Norwegian as possible, while also feeling like you're inching closer to grasping the language at a higher level. For this reason, informal lessons are a great starting point for anyone, regardless of your level.

2. Structured lessons: If you want a more structured approach to learning, using books might be the way to go. "På Vei" and "Stein På Stein" are both excellent resources to learn Norwegian and understand more about Norway. With these lessons, I also give homework and correct written texts you send me after class.

1. Try reading the chapter we're going through before or after our lesson. Try to get a sense of what the chapter is about.

2. Read Norwegian articles, listen to podcasts or watch TV shows.
